channel.title: The No-Tell Motel
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "The No-Tell Motel" - A seemingly unassuming roadside Motel in the Mojave Desert is actually a fixed point that exist in multiple realities.

item.title: Re: The No-Tell Motel
item.content:encoded:
Haha. Any of these reasons would be plausible and interesting to explore. You just need to pick one and weave the backstory into your logs. Like you said as well, all the Staff need to do is hint and let pieces of info slip - you don't have to detail the backstory for it to work.

The dragons tho…. heh. That sounds a bit random atm. But if you can find a way to include it earlier on in the article, why not? Anyway, here's your greenlight. The concept is ambitious but more importantly, it sounds interesting and worth a read once it's done. Do send me the draft once you get your second greenlight - would love to read it.

Best of luck!

item.title: Re: The No-Tell Motel
item.content:encoded:
Hiya Caspian2!

I see. Okay. Perhaps the origin of the Motel is a chain of motels, which no longer exist and almost all records of such a chain seem to have vanished, with very few actually capable of remembering them. And that all of the motels were constructed exactly the same way, and made and furnished inside and outside in a way that made them all identical! And what caused them all to disappear from almost all records was the new mysterious owners purchasing the entire chain! Maybe they could be… dragons? Interdimensional dragons that expanded into different universes for their own version of a chain?

As for the reason why. One theory can be that it's part of an ongoing experiment on the different guests and worlds. Another is that it's a form of entertainment, like a kind of reality show, for them! OH! One of the Staff could even let slip something to that effect, or at least their own theory about it. Yet another theory is that they are doing this in preparation for a multi-dimensional event/crisis that the "dragons" see coming!

(In addition to dragons, I LOVE Rick and Morty and their Interdimensional Cable episodes, as well as the Morty's Mindblowers and the strange train episode!)

item.title: Re: The No-Tell Motel
item.content:encoded:
Hi Gryphon Watcher, thank you for your elaboration.

It's origins are unknown, and if the staff know they are refusing to answer, but it's goal seems to be to draw in "guests", in some cases with an intent to give them anomalous properties/abilities.

Hmm. This is still the part that's problematic for me. You've described A LOT of various anomalous properties that the hotel manifests, and I get that it's a place of intersecting universes, so this kind of randomness is to be expected.

But you need to have an explanation for the base anomaly. What exactly are its origins, and why does it want to draw guests in and turn them into anomalies themselves. I feel that if you were to explore this strand further, this will be your Central Narrative and the basis of your breaching and exploration logs. The Foundation has to investigate the anomaly and ultimately reach a conclusion of sorts. What is this conclusion?

Right now, the description sounds very cool, but it also sounds like an episode of Interdimensional Cable from Rick & Morty (you should check it out). While it's cool for a while to see random things happening, there has to be an underlying narrative that ties things together. Otherwise, it's just a series of random occurences and there's no payoff.

For what it's worth, I think you're on the right track, and you're close to a greenlight from me. Continue expanding on what the end goal of the article will look like?

item.title: Re: The No-Tell Motel
item.content:encoded:
The exploration logs involve singular as well as small groups of D-Class personnel, as well as scientists with armed escorts. They will do things like talk to the staff and try to get pictures of them (which are always blurry on the faces of said staff) and try to map out the endless halls, which seems to shift suddenly, but not in any perceptible way. Also, I figure that they would also try sending in a drone like with the Endless Ikea. The exploration logs will all involve those who enter having a very hard time finding their way back to the front desk and exit. Sometimes they find it on their own, other times the staff or security helps them, and sometimes they are never heard from again. They even sometimes return with individuals who have been lost for years. Some of then come from alternate Earths. There are even others who, while not appearing human, insist that they are human, and that their strange appearances is normal on the Earth they are from. Also, some of those who leave have anomalous properties/abilities, having been altered by the motel through an event that they cannot recall the details of. The log will also include encounters with the entities from the various worlds viewed from the rooms through the windows.

+ Open
- Close

And for the breach log, that will be similar to the exploration log, in that those who check in will sometimes find their way back out on their own, be escorted by the staff, or disappear, sometimes forever. Of course, there will be the accounts of on-site personnel trying to apprehend them. Some will be from them trying to drive onto the site, being turned away in a daze. Others will insist that they have an appointment at the motel, even becoming belligerent and/or violent. (One such example of that being the entire biker gang that drove up claiming to have an appointment.) This will be a daily occurrence of at least two or three instances. But then there are others that, as though the fence surrounding it weren't there, drove into the parking lot, always when no one was observing. Those are always surprised to be caught, if the on-site personnel can get to them in time, completely oblivious to being in a restricted area. That's a bit rarer. Once every couple of months or so. And then, there's said on-site personnel who, for reasons that they themselves cannot remember, also try to check in.

As for it's nature… well, it's (theorized) a fixed point in many different alternate universes that exists as is, despite being in locations where it makes no sense for a motel like itself to exist in. (I.e. the bottom of an ocean, near an altar, in a swamp, etc.) It's origins are unknown, and if the staff know they are refusing to answer, but it's goal seems to be to draw in "guests", in some cases with an intent to give them anomalous properties/abilities. Said abilities are seemingly random.

item.title: Re: The No-Tell Motel
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Gryphon Watcher. Let’s take a look at your concept.

So your Elevator Pitch has gotten me intrigued. It sorta reminds me of the Interdimensional Diner in SCP-4258. There are loads of opportunities to take such a concept and I’m also glad to see you playing around with some of those ideas with manipulating the physical space and thinking about its inhabitants.

Central Narrative: World-building

I don’t understand what you mean by this, though. If you mean ‘world-building’ as description of the setting, I’m afraid that’s not the same thing as having an actual storyline for us to follow. Are you planning on having an exploration log? How will you be showing us around the hotel? Even SCP-4258 had distinct characters that followed through each time the Foundation visited – who do we meet at your hotel besides an assortment of guests?

That’s my main issue at the moment: it’s not enough to simply have a cool setting. What are you going to do with it, who are the main characters involved and why are the stakes high enough for the Foundation to get involved? I hope you can elaborate on these pointers.

If you decide to revise your concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll do my best to reply. All the best for now!

item.title: The No-Tell Motel
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, (Some) Comedy, Sci-Fi

Page Layout (Optional): Article Format

+ Open
- Close

Elevator Pitch:

⦁ A seemingly unassuming small hotel in the Mojave Desert

⦁ The interior is infinitely larger than the exterior

⦁ The motel is a fixed point in multiple realities

⦁ There's no observable staff from outside, but inside there is

⦁ Those who have seen the staff cannot recall any physical features, only that they are polite and courteous

⦁ Some staff have personalities that can be recalled, but that is the only memorable trait they have

⦁ Those who stay past check out are escorted out by security, also whose features are unable to be recalled

⦁ Occasionally, those that check in are altered to have an anomalous ability/property, and it is hinted by the staff that that's one of the reasons why they are drawn in

⦁ The halls are infinite and labyrinthine

⦁ The motel rooms are generic and normal-seeming

⦁ The motel room windows each look out on different worlds

⦁ Some people who leave the motel are from alternate Earths

⦁ Despite the monitoring and security, somehow, sometimes some people manage to get past to check in

⦁ An exploration log will be included, detailing science teams with armed escorts as well as D-class personnel teams exploring the Motel's interior

⦁ A breach log which will detail instances where civilians attempt to gain entry to the site, have gained entry, as well as those who managed to make it into the motel. This log will also include instances where those who entered are recovered. It will also detail instances where on-site personnel themselves attempted to check in to the motel.

Central Narrative: World-building

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The motel occasionally has a guest who stays in a room that looks out onto our world, and the dressers are filled with money from different time periods and countries, some of which no longer exist or have never existed. And the money includes ancient drachmas, crudely carved red painted stones, and etc.

Additional Notes: I'm not sure where I need help, but I gladly accept any advice willing to be given!
